newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro Q2 earnings show turnaround-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Vitro Q2 earnings show turnaround-analysts.

text.p: Mexican glassmaker Vitro's recent second quarter earnings showed the company may finally be out of trouble, analysts said.
Vitro posted net earnings of 196 million pesos for the second quarter on July 10, compared with a loss of 1.027 billion pesos for the same quarter last year.
Analysts said the main reason for the turnaround was that Vitro shed loss-making subsidiary Anchor Glass Corp in February.
"Vitro is out of hot water now," said Urban Larson, an analyst with Salomon Brothers in Mexico.

"The report had few surprises, as it was expected to be good, above all due to the Domestic Appliances division," he added, referring to a new refrigerator plant Vitro opened in northern industrial state Nuevo Leon.
For Sandra Morfin of Santander Investment in Mexico, Vitro's earnings showed a mixed improvement.
"Operating earnings and margin were better than I was expecting, but the net line was below consensus due to a write-down for Serfin we were not expecting this quarter," she said.
Vitro currently has a 11.4 percent stake in the Serfin financial group.
Morfin said extraordinary earnings from the sale of Vitro's Raw Materials division helped offset the write down from Serfin.
A New York analyst, who asked not to be named, noted Vitro had managed to increase sales in year-on-year terms "despite the relative strength of the peso against the dollar."
